doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Worries about the future audience for pre-bebop jazz
summary: He fears the audience is aging with no younger listeners and calls for music appreciation courses.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Right, that’s okay. How do you feel about the future of this music — well I’m not sure what I mean by “this music” but—

I’m worried to the point of ulcers about it. Because as our audience gets older I don’t see a younger one coming up. There are plenty of youth education programs to teach young people to play this music, I don’t know who they’re going to play it for. I don’t know of music appreciation courses or even public concerts to get more people interested in a style from Buddy Bolden to Bunny Berrigan. I mean the kids are going to have to find it on their own and say wow I’d like to play trumpet like that, and then in 2025 I’ll say © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

good luck. I hope someone’s there to listen to it. That really worries me. I mean you can see the age of the audience here, and they’re great supporters, they go to all these things, they buy the recordings, they’re the salt of the earth, but when they’re gone, I don’t know. And it’s the same with the jazz festivals that I play on the west coast — the Dixieland festivals. An older crowd. If you add other music to bring in a younger crowd, you can add Zydeco and blues and Cajun music and things like that, but that’s not jazz, that’s not teaching them to appreciate Freddie Keppard or Bix or Earl Hines. So I don’t know the answer to that except music appreciation courses starting right now, in as many places as possible.

Because there’ll always be someone who’ll say well I like that, I don’t care to play it, I’d rather fiddle with my computer but I like the music and I’d go to hear it. I mean I hope that turns out that way.
Yeah we definitely need more audience.
